qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: High switching costs and participant inertia in employer-sponsored defined contribution / 401(k) retirement plans and target-date fund suites provide a sticky asset base. However, this moat is actively eroding due to structural disintermediation and counter-positioning from low-cost passive index giants (Vanguard, BlackRock iShares) and fee compression across the active equity industry. Operating ROIC remains historically healthy (~18-20%), but pricing power is non-existent as effective fee rates have declined to 38.8 bps alongside persistent annual net asset outflows.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Pricing Power & Proof of Moat, REJECT). While T. Rowe Price maintains high switching costs in corporate 401(k) retirement plan administration and target-date fund franchises, it possesses zero pricing power above inflation. The firm faces relentless secular migration from active equity management to passive low-cost index funds and ETFs, driving cumulative net outflows ($43.2B in 2024, $56.9B in 2025) and continuous effective fee rate compression from 41.9 bps in 2023 to 41.0 bps in 2024 and 38.8 bps in 2025. Any attempt to raise fee rates accelerates client redemption.
qualitative.evidence: Empirical track record shows sustained ROIC (~18.5% 10-year median) and an unblemished fortress balance sheet with zero core long-term debt and >$3B in cash and discretionary seed investments. However, organic growth has turned permanently negative in core active equities: net client outflows reached $81.8B in 2022, ~$80B in 2023, $43.2B in 2024, and $56.9B in 2025 despite market tailwinds expanding total AUM to $1.78T. Average effective fee rate compressed from 41.9 bps in 2023 to 41.0 bps in 2024 and 38.8 bps in 2025. FCF conversion remains high (~$1.3B-$2.0B annually), but inability to raise fees or stem active equity outflows demonstrates the complete absence of pricing power >= inflation.
